title: Dating and Placing the Measurement
summary: Work through Dating and Placing the Measurement.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Dating and Placing the Measurement**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Sensor Perception, § Dating and Placing the Measurement
blocks.md: A frame from the navigation camera lands in host memory as an array of pixel values. Nothing in that array says when the light was captured, where the camera was mounted, or how far a position read from it can be trusted, yet the planner that checks rack-end clearance needs all three. Every modality has the same gap. A trajectory optimizer cannot plan against unorganized time-of-flight returns, and a force controller cannot track a grid of raw intensities.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Capture epoch matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A measurement is dated at its exposure midpoint or per-point firing time, never at arrival, and rolling-shutter rows and LiDAR sweeps sample the scene at different instants that capture-time geometry must undo.

questions.q: The section **Dating and Placing the Measurement** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Each oscillator stamps time in its own clock domain, so a capture time can be checked only after conversion to the consumer's clock, and that conversion carries a measured bound (offset tail, path asymmetry, drift between syncs) that every age check adds.
Out-of-distribution and input-support monitors flag into the health bitmask and can demote a camera to LiDAR-only operation, but they cannot certify what the transducer itself got wrong.

Learned depth and semantic confidence are not metric evidence, so a learned head may classify and propose but the range that enters a clearance check comes from qualified metric sensing, which can veto.

A measurement is dated at its exposure midpoint or per-point firing time, never at arrival, and rolling-shutter rows and LiDAR sweeps sample the scene at different instants that capture-time geometry must undo.
